tasks.title: Navier–Stokes reconstruction
tasks.aim: Reconstruct and audit OpenAI's public 8 September 2026 Navier–Stokes release, FINITE TIME BLOWUP FOR NAVIER–STOKES (165-page manuscript; formal companion pinned at openai/NavierStokesAndEuler@8937a8f4cbc7abaab5e9e97d1cc7f5d2319d9538). The source claims a classical 3D forced Navier–Stokes solution with positive viscosity, zero initial velocity, smooth compactly supported forcing, bounded kinetic energy, and a terminal unbounded-velocity event; this account records reconstruction status, not independent certification.
tasks.broader_motivation: The concrete source sequence is: leading profiles (manuscript §4 and App. B), base/heat correction (§5 and App. A), oscillatory velocity/shear fields (§§6–7 and App. C), mean corrections (§8), finite correction cycle (§9), and endpoint/localization (§10). Naming those objects lets the reader distinguish what was reconstructed from what remains unverified.

tasks.title: S6 geometry and marked lattice constructions
tasks.aim: Inspect the claimed complex-threefold construction on S^6 circulated by Levent Alpöge with Fable, using the frozen key-advances reader and complete archive (Zenodo 22678442), while separating geometric certificates from broader physical interpretations.
tasks.broader_motivation: The calculations ask whether the proposed fibration, period deformation, finite fillings, and marked cubic lattices are intrinsic and exact. They do not turn the geometric construction into a Yang–Mills or mass-gap theorem.
tasks.coverage: Five selected routes in the published key-advances reader; not the entire historical S6 workbench.

attempts.title: Recover the fibration from the threefold
attempts.aim: Identify the fibration intrinsically so deformations of the whole threefold can be tested.
attempts.rationale: The canonical sections can encode the base map rather than just a chosen marked fibre.
attempts.rationale_basis: The source explicitly explains this as the purpose of the intrinsic fibration calculation.
attempts.tried: Calculated the evaluation zero divisor, canonical powers and full graded anticanonical algebra in the original coordinates.
attempts.outcome: The record gives an explicit degree-two map recovering the fibration up to its retained projective-coordinate choice.
attempts.extent: A result for the specified analytic construction and its hypotheses; not independent validation of every step of the original S6 claim.
attempts.brief: For the claimed complex threefold on S^6, we tested whether the fibration is recoverable from the threefold rather than chosen as an external coordinate. Canonical sections and the full anticanonical graded algebra give an explicit degree-two map with the original projective coordinates retained. This is a certificate for the specified analytic construction.

evidence.section: 1. The anticanonical ring recovers the fibration; full proof Theorem 53.17, CR1–CR5

attempts.title: Vary the original period parameter
attempts.aim: Determine whether the retained period parameter gives a nonzero deformation of the whole threefold.
attempts.rationale: A nonzero regular-fibre variation can be carried to the whole space if the intrinsic fibration and its three critical values control possible trivializations.
attempts.rationale_basis: Source-based reconstruction of the displayed local-to-global proof strategy.
attempts.tried: Kept the original period matrices, computed the marked coordinate and Kodaira–Spencer maps, and used the intrinsic fibration to test first-order triviality.
attempts.outcome: The record proves a nonzero global first-order deformation in the stated parameter region.
attempts.extent: It does not classify all deformations or prove every two parameters yield nonisomorphic unmarked manifolds.
attempts.brief: We varied the S^6 construction's original period parameter and computed the period and Kodaira–Spencer maps. The intrinsic fibration and three fixed critical values give a nonzero first-order fibre variation. This does not classify all deformations or distinguish every pair of unmarked fibres.

evidence.section: 2. The original period constant gives a nonzero deformation; Theorem 53.18, PD1–PD18

attempts.aim: Compare the cyclic octonionic Leech construction with the two retained embedded lattices on their actual common points.
attempts.rationale: An exact intersection in the unchanged Cayley coordinates can test a relationship that abstract lattice isometry alone does not determine.
attempts.rationale_basis: Editorial reconstruction from the literal-intersection calculation.
attempts.tried: Computed both intersections in the original frame, their Gram data, and the cubic values on that common lattice.

tasks.title: Zeta and arithmetic transport routes
tasks.aim: Reconstruct the frozen 411-page zeta reader (Zenodo 22678086) and its complete source archive, then test explicit Weil, Mellin, angular-momentum, and radial-recursion claims without treating a transported signal as an RH proof.
tasks.broader_motivation: The route keeps the actual polynomial mechanism, theta input, corrected fluid field, full Mellin factors, and axis recursion named. This makes clear which calculations are exact source results and which RH-relevant conclusions remain unproved.
tasks.coverage: Selected routes documented in the frozen 411-page main reader; not an exhaustive account of the literature corpus or every sidebar, and not a statement that later work does not exist.

attempts.title: Keep the branches, then transport the equations
attempts.aim: Carry the supplied polynomial mechanism into fluid and arithmetic coordinates without losing inverse branches.
attempts.rationale: Its inverse-fibre geometry exposes precisely where projection loses information.
attempts.rationale_basis: reconstructed_from_written_argument
attempts.tried: Constructed the full cubic inverse chart, exceptional fibres, incompressible trajectories and transformed diffusion operators.
attempts.outcome: Obtained exact maps and an escaping trajectory in the retained pullback metric.
attempts.extent: That metric is incomplete; this route did not itself produce a classical Euclidean Navier–Stokes singularity or an off-critical zeta zero. The later work therefore also uses the actual released fluid field.
attempts.brief: In the frozen zeta reader's retained polynomial mechanism (satellites/23_source_mechanism_transfer.tex), we kept inverse branches, exceptional fibres, and diffusion maps while transporting the equations into fluid and arithmetic coordinates. The pullback metric has an escaping trajectory but is incomplete; no classical Euclidean fluid singularity or off-critical zeta zero follows.

attempts.title: Test the negative coefficient in the complete Weil form

attempts.rationale: The retained coefficient acts on the actual theta input whose Fourier transform is Xi.

attempts.tried: Evaluated the complete Weil form, retaining pole, gamma and prime-power terms, cross terms and infinite-tail bounds.
attempts.outcome: The recorded certified value is positive, approximately 2.0984855607004 × 10⁻¹¹.
attempts.extent: This particular input is not a negative Weil witness. The calculation neither proves global Weil positivity nor settles RH; the negative linear coefficient remains a different, explicitly related calculation.

The source records a positive value, about 2.0984855607004 × 10^-19, so this input is not a negative witness; global Weil positivity and RH remain unsettled.

attempts.title: Transport the actual concentrating swirl into arithmetic
attempts.aim: Propagate the released corrected fluid field itself, rather than infer its behaviour from an analogy.
attempts.rationale: Angular momentum retains a concentrating source component and admits explicit dilation and Mellin maps.

attempts.outcome: The written calculation obtains a directly growing arithmetic derivative and an equal genuine Mellin residue at s = −1.
attempts.extent: This is a precise transported signal, not an off-critical zeta zero. Independent verification of the imported complete source existence theorem is unfinished.

The calculation gives a growing arithmetic derivative and matching Mellin residue at s=-1. This is a transported source signal, not an off-critical zeta zero; independent validation of the imported source theorem remains unfinished.

attempts.title: Recover data hidden by trivial-zero cancellation
attempts.aim: Find where higher radial information goes when a zeta factor cancels its Mellin pole.
attempts.rationale: A cancelled pole need not mean that the input coefficient has disappeared.
attempts.rationale_basis: reconstructed_from_written_argument
attempts.tried: Expanded the full Mellin product at negative integers and retained the local zeta factors.
attempts.outcome: Odd Taylor coefficients are recovered from residues; even coefficients from regular values divided by the nonzero derivative of the multiplier.
attempts.extent: This recovers the complete Taylor sequence, not an arbitrary smooth germ from that sequence alone. Flat remainders remain in the full invertible transform; no new nontrivial zeta zero is obtained.
attempts.brief: We expanded the full Mellin product at negative integers to track data hidden when a zeta factor cancels a pole. Odd Taylor coefficients come from residues and even coefficients from regular values divided by the nonzero multiplier derivative. This recovers the Taylor sequence, not an arbitrary smooth germ; flat remainders remain.

attempts.title: Make the higher radial source data constructive
attempts.aim: Extend the axis calculation beyond its first derivative without replacing the complete corrected field.
attempts.rationale: The preceding second-coefficient cancellation suggested finite source dependence at each fixed radial degree.
attempts.rationale_basis: reconstructed_from_written_argument
attempts.tried: Derived the coupled coefficient recursion with pressure, viscosity and cutoff terms, then carried it into residue/value coordinates.
attempts.outcome: The written induction gives vanishing above correction order n > m and a finite algorithm for every fixed Taylor degree.
attempts.extent: This is not convergence of the uncut series or an autonomous finite-dimensional fluid system. The full functions, nonlinear fluxes and flat remainders remain necessary.
attempts.brief: We extended the corrected fluid field's axis calculation beyond its first radial derivative, retaining pressure, viscosity, cutoff, and Mellin residue/value terms. The written induction gives vanishing above correction order n>m and a finite algorithm at each fixed degree. It does not prove convergence of the uncut series or produce an autonomous finite-dimensional fluid system.
